title: Adrenal Steroid Converter
description: Converts between equivalent glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid doses of commonly used adrenal steroids.
purpose: Used to converts between equivalent glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid doses of commonly used adrenal steroids.

advice: Use equivalent doses when switching between glucocorticoids to avoid under- or over-treatment.
Biological half-life matters: dexamethasone and betamethasone are long-acting and carry higher risk of HPA axis suppression.
When transitioning to hydrocortisone for adrenal insufficiency, consider physiological cortisol rhythm (higher morning dose).
warnings: These are approximate equivalences; individual patient response may vary.
Conversion does not account for mineralocorticoid activity (hydrocortisone has significant mineralocorticoid effect; dexamethasone has none).
Long-term steroid use at any dose increases risk of osteoporosis, diabetes, and infections.
followUp: Monitor blood glucose, bone density, and blood pressure during prolonged glucocorticoid therapy.
When tapering, reduce gradually to allow HPA axis recovery.
Consider steroid-sparing agents in autoimmune or inflammatory conditions.

faq.question: How do I convert prednisone to dexamethasone?
faq.answer: Prednisone 5 mg is approximately equivalent to dexamethasone 0.75 mg. Divide the prednisone dose by approximately 6.67 to get the dexamethasone equivalent.

faq.question: Why is hydrocortisone used for adrenal insufficiency?
faq.answer: Hydrocortisone has both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid activity, making it the preferred replacement in adrenal insufficiency when given in divided doses to mimic physiological cortisol rhythm.

faq.question: Are steroid equivalences exact?
faq.answer: No. These are approximations based on anti-inflammatory potency. Individual patient response varies based on metabolism, comorbidities, and the specific clinical condition.
